items.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003
items.q: When a guy like Stevie Wonder can’t come up with a hit, you know he’s a real songwriter.

ctx.x: So you know, if that human being came out of my string ballad concert — I mean there were actually people weeping in the concert. There’s something about strings that can make you go into it. But the whole thing is to do it without being maudlin. It can be contrived. You know strings, you can be cornball city with strings too, especially if you approach it from the ballad thing. Anyway, and that’s the whole thing about melody and song form, there’s a battle in the society right now because everybody’s more…

I look forward to that too. Yeah. It’s interesting when you think about what are the songs — I occasionally play like weddings and stuff. And people seem to be, even young people now, gravitating toward the older songs, because what can they pick that’s current to play at a function like that.
